units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 4:6:2">Y. B. Bath. IV, 14ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>בית הכ׳ שלעצים</he> a store-house for wood (= <cite ref="A00825"><he>אוֹצָר</he></cite>).
Ex. R. s. 21 (interch. with preced. w.); Yalk. Ps. 840, v. preced.—בית הכ׳ (abbr. בה״כ) synagogue.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 3:1">Meg. III, 1</cite> (<cite ref="Megillah 25b">25ᵇ</cite>); a. fr.—

Sot. VII, 7 חזן הכ׳ the sexton of the synagogue within the Temple precincts; Succ. 51ᵇ of the synagogue of Alexandria, v. חַזָּן; a. fr.—כ׳ ישראל (abbrev. כ״י) the congregation of Israel, the Ecclesia, (often personified as a woman betrothed to the Lord).
Cant. R. to I, 4; a. fr.—כ׳ הגדולה (abbr. כה״ג) the Great Assembly, Ecclesia or Synagoga Magna, a supreme authority established under Ezra and Nehemiah.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:1">Ab. I, 1</cite>, a. fr. <he>אנשי כ׳ הג׳</he> the men of the original Great Synagogue.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>שירי כה״ג</he> the last members of the Great Synagogue.—Pl. <he>כְּנֵסִיּוֹת</he>, <he>כְּנֵיסִ׳</he>. Lam. R. introd. (R. Yitsḥ. 3) <he>בני כְּנֵסִיּוֹתָיו</he> his fellow-members in the royal council; (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 318">Yalk. Is. 318</cite> <he>בני המלך</he>).—<he>בתי כ׳</he> synagogues.
<cite ref="Megillah 6a:14">Meg. 6ᵃ</cite>. Y. ib. III, beg. 73ᵈ <he>ארבע … ב׳ כ׳ וכ׳</he> there were four hundred and eighty synagogues in Jerusalem, and each had a school &c.
<cite ref="Chullin 51a:5">Ḥull. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>מפטיר כ׳</he> janitor at meetings of scholars in college.
<cite ref="Pesachim 49b:2">Pes. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>ראשי כ׳</he> chiefs of congregations or synagogues.
